Preparing for the civil service exam, I barely have time to sit at my desk, and every time I see the pile of dishes after a meal, I sigh deeply. Plus, in the middle of winter, if the sink doesn't have hot water, I hate dipping my hands in cold water. Hoping to escape this dishwashing hell, I finally decided to look into a dishwasher. I placed it in a corner of the kitchen, and the clean white tones and transparent window design brightened the kitchen. Watching the water circulate inside, gently washing the dishes, is strangely soothing and refreshing. I thought it would be small for three people, but it easily holds the day's worth of dishes, a daily tumbler, and a small pot if you're good at Tetris. It's a truly golden size for a single-person household. Powerful cleaning and UV sterilization. Perfectly removes grease! Hygiene is also a concern. This was my first dishwasher, so I was worried that the rice might not be cleaned properly, but my worries were completely unfounded. It washes thoroughly with super-hot water, and even the grease from the meat is perfectly removed. It makes a squeaky-squeaky sound when touched. It even sterilizes thoroughly with UV light after each wash, so I can use my spoons and cups without worrying about germs, which is a huge plus for hygiene. Learning one more word during dishwashing has really improved my quality of life. Overall Review. A compact three-person size that fits comfortably in even the smallest kitchen. This is a must-have item for test-takers, allowing them to sit down at their desks and study right after eating. It's a bit noisy when it's running, with the water circulating and draining. --------------. If you find this helpful, you'll have a wonderful week :)

Sentence (English): I replaced my beloved Kitchen Aid with a Bosch, chosen because it has great revies for reliability in CR.
Comments (English): [ Overall, happy with the dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I replaced my beloved Kitchen Aid with a Bosch, chosen because it has great revies for reliability in CR. As with most things, there's a period of adaptation but overall have no regrets. First and most importantly, the dishes are clean and it seems to get most of the difficult stuff (dried dog food) on the first try without much pre-rinsing. And if it does not konk out after 5 years, I will be happy. But there are a few ridiculous engineering oversights. I passed on a Bosch many years ago because the racking system is not well designed for a mixed load of plates and bowls. I can't put cereal or pasta or cat food, etc. bowls in the racks (tines too close) and when I set them along the sides or on the middle rack, the plates bump up against them, the dishwasher is full after one meal, and the bowls are not secure through the cycle. The silverware caddy is ridiculously small, does not have a separate open area for small non-utensil items such bottle stoppers, etc. And the start/etc. buttons are confusing. To choose your cycle, you must hit "Restart." (Why not "On" or "Select Cycle"? Ironically, there is a restart process but that button alone does not control it! ) There is a "clean" light so you know when the dishes are clean -- mine does not work and judging from other reviews, nobody else has a working one either. (One reviewer said it goes on for 30 seconds following a cycle ---but we cannot see it because it is under the counter.) I can't easily tell whether the dishes are clean when I come down in the morning since by then, the light is off. I want one that stays on until I acknowledge it! The remote start has to be reset every single time you want to use it remotely (or perhaps I am doing it wrong, but no manual on this and the QR links do not adequately explain the use of remote start). And the dishwasher is either tightly latched, or it is open 3-4 inches and gets in my way. I keep it open to prevent mildew, and would greatly prefer if the door didn't jut out into the kitchen all the time, but there is no way to get it to sit open just a hair. The dishwasher works quietly, efficiently, and overall there is a lot I love about it. But I wish the engineers listened to consumers before they settled on this design because it could have been a GREAT dishwasher with a few inexpensive adjustments.

Sentence (English): Purchased in Jan 2026.
Comments (English): [ Don't waste your money ] || ---------------- || Purchased in Jan 2026. Purchased the 800 based on reviews especially drying ability. Watched numerous videos on setting to use and how to load dishwasher. Top dish rack is not designed right. Hard to place bowls so they remain upright. Then very little room for glasses. Bowls use to go right down the center. Not on this machine. They go to the left side of rack, as shown in videos. This leaves less room for glasses wear. I've used the dishwasher sample soap that comes with it and tried powder soap. I also filled rinse aid with product recommended. Loading the dishwasher without rinsing off dishes prior to loading as instructed. Of course big stuff comes off before loading. The plates come out fine however the glass ware comes out with flim on them. I've adjusted the amount of rise aid dispensed also. Are home water goes through waterboy system so I'm not using unfiltered water. So I am stumped why the dishes don't come out perfect, especially for something that cost 1300.00 dollars. So save your money and buys something less expensive and will most likely work just as good or better

Sentence (English): So far so good!
Comments (English): [ Great features and amazingly quiet! ] || ---------------- || So far so good! This dishwasher is a huge improvement over our old (19 years old in fact) Whirlpool. The biggest differences are: (1) it's so quiet we can barely hear it running! And (2) it has plenty of space with a third rack. And of course, it does a great job cleaning dishes even if they haven't been fully pre-rinsed, though I usually wipe them off or give them a quick rinse. The only negatives: touch controls at the top of the door are highly sensitive and I often activate one by accident, just opening or closing the door. I'm also not thrilled with having to remove spoons and forks by touching the "business end" but they do get cleaner that way; if it were really an issue I could wear gloves. And the adjustable rack takes a little getting used to. It will probably be fine once I'm more familiar with it.
